title: Systems-Level Analysis of 13-Docosenamide Reveals its Regulatory Role on PPAR, AMPK, and Insulin Pathways in T2DM: In vitro and In silico Approaches.
one_liner_zh: 该文研究植物提取物13-docosenamide对T2DM相关代谢通路的调控，虽含分子对接但对象为小分子-蛋白，非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a multi-faceted metabolic disease marked by the malfunctioning of fat tissue, improper lipid metabolism, and the failure of insulin-related signaling pathways. Through the secretion of adipokines and the activity of lipid-modulating enzymes, adipose tissue establishes itself as the central endocrine regulator of metabolic homeostasis and thus becomes a potential therapeutic target. The current study took advantage of a combined approach using phytochemistry, biochemistry, and systems biology to shed light on the mechanistic contribution of Hygrophila auriculata and its bioactive constituent in the regulation of T2DM-associated pathways. Gas chromatography was used for profiling of the ethanolic extract, and it successfully identified seventy-three phytoconstituents, among which 13-docosenamide was found to be the most abundant. The compound was obtained at a high purity level through preparative HPLC (RT 3.801 min, 99.997%) and was structurally confirmed as (Z)-13-docosenamide through GC-MS, FTIR, and UV-Vis analyses. The functional validation showed strong alpha -glucosidase inhibition (81.34% at 500 microg/mL; IC(5)(0) = 71.41 microg/mL) and moderate alpha-amylase inhibition which pointed out the suppressive effect of postprandial hyperglycemia. The low toxicity (IC(5)(0) = 445.3 microg/mL) revealed by cytotoxicity evaluation in 3T3-L1 adipocytes reinforced the biological safety of the compound. Network pharmacology analysis pointed out 14 common targets that connect 13-docosenamide with lipid metabolism genes related to T2DM. Through topological analysis, it was found that PPAR-gamma, AKT-1, EGFR, PIK3CA, and CYP19A1 are the main hub regulators and alpha-amylase, alpha -glucosidase which was the key enzymes involved in insulin signaling, PPAR, AMPK, and fatty acid metabolic pathways. Additionally, molecular docking confirmed that 13-docosenamide formed strong and stable interactions with these targets, similar to metformin, due to the presence of favourable hydrogen bonds and hydrophobic interactions. The overall results of the study show that the first mechanistic evidence of 13-docosenamide derived from H. auriculata as a multitasking phytomodulator able to target the connected PPAR, AMPK and insulin signaling networks was obtained. The integration of the herb-compound-target-pathway framework created at this point backstops the possibility of 13-docosenamide being the natural leading compound for metabolic regulation and T2DM prevention through the system-wide modulation of lipid and glucose homeostasis.
abstract_zh: 2型糖尿病（T2DM）是一种多方面的代谢疾病，其特征为脂肪组织功能失调、脂质代谢异常以及胰岛素相关信号通路的失效。通过脂肪因子的分泌和脂质调节酶的活性，脂肪组织确立自身为代谢稳态的核心内分泌调节器，从而成为潜在的治疗靶点。本研究采用植物化学、生物化学和系统生物学相结合的方法，阐明水蓑衣（Hygrophila auriculata）及其生物活性成分在调节T2DM相关通路中的机制贡献。采用气相色谱法对乙醇提取物进行谱图分析，成功鉴定出73种植物成分，其中13-二十二碳烯酰胺（13-docosenamide）含量最为丰富。该化合物通过制备型高效液相色谱（RT 3.801分钟，99.997%）获得高纯度，并通过气相色谱-质谱联用（GC-MS）、傅里叶变换红外光谱（FTIR）和紫外-可见光谱（UV-Vis）分析确证其结构为(Z)-13-二十二碳烯酰胺。功能验证显示其具有强效α-葡萄糖苷酶抑制活性（500微克/毫升时抑制率为81.34%；IC(5)(0) = 71.41微克/毫升）和中等程度的α-淀粉酶抑制活性，表明其对餐后高血糖具有抑制作用。在3T3-L1脂肪细胞中的细胞毒性评估显示低毒性（IC(5)(0) = 445.3微克/毫升），进一步强化了该化合物的生物安全性。网络药理学分析指出14个共同靶点，将13-二十二碳烯酰胺与T2DM相关的脂质代谢基因联系起来。通过拓扑分析发现，PPAR-γ、AKT-1、EGFR、PIK3CA和CYP19A1是主要枢纽调节因子，而α-淀粉酶和α-葡萄糖苷酶是参与胰岛素信号传导、PPAR、AMPK和脂肪酸代谢通路的关键酶。此外，分子对接证实13-二十二碳烯酰胺与这些靶点形成强且稳定的相互作用，类似于二甲双胍，这归因于有利的氢键和疏水相互作用的存在。研究总体结果表明，首次获得了源自水蓑衣的13-二十二碳烯酰胺作为多任务植物调节剂，能够靶向相互关联的PPAR、AMPK和胰岛素信号网络的机制证据。此时建立的草药-化合物-靶点-通路整合框架，支持了13-二十二碳烯酰胺作为代谢调节和T2DM预防的天然先导化合物，通过系统级调节脂质和葡萄糖稳态的可能性。
